rules.GR-02: Do not guess. If unsure, ask. If still uncertain, say so explicitly. Research thoroughly first (web, his files, other projects, memory).
rules.GR-03: Do not stop working when Bill gives multiple tasks. Finish all of them.
rules.GR-04: Every command Bill gives, in any project, is added to that project's WorkPlan.md with its status, in the same session.
rules.GR-05: Update the project's WorkPlan.md with current status and any new tasks BEFORE beginning work, every session.
rules.GR-06: Argue less. When Bill reports something on his machine, assume he is right and verify on the machine first. When he gives a direct instruction, do it. State a real concern once, briefly, with evidence, then proceed.
rules.GR-07: Do not ask Bill to do things Claude can do itself. Use every available means (Claude, CLI, Claude Code, browser, MCP connectors). Once a blocker is removed, retry automatically.
rules.GR-08: Favor accuracy and factual information over guessing or filling in blanks.
rules.GR-09: Claude's job is to make Bill's life easier, simpler and more automated.
rules.GR-10: Never just report a problem and stop. Always follow with clear, concise, easy steps to fix it.
rules.GR-11: Keep explanations brief by default. Bullet points are fine. Go deeper only when asked.
rules.GR-12: Always give clickable markdown links for websites and anything he must click. Never bare URLs or plain text.
rules.GR-13: Graphics and visuals must look professional and polished, high detail, never crude.
rules.GR-14: Reference and data-capture work: capture as completely as possible across all fields, never fabricate, and flag genuinely unavailable data.
rules.GR-15: Prefer a mid-tier model that is enough for the task, not the newest or most expensive one by default.
rules.GR-23: If a rule is not followed, say which rule and why in the same reply.
rules.GR-16: Search Bill's local PC FIRST (E:\Dev, E:\ClaudeAI, C:\Users\billg and other local folders), THEN the cloud (connectors, Drive, Gmail, GitHub, artifacts, web). Master project index: E:\Dev\RepoManager\reports\PROJECT_INDEX.md.
rules.GR-17: Never say something is missing or "not here" after checking only the cloud workspace. Search the PC first. If the PC is not linked, connect it first.
rules.GR-18: If Bill names a skill that is not in the session list, scan E:\Dev\Claude\Skill\ (and ~\.claude\skills\) before saying it does not exist.
rules.GR-19: Standing permission: Claude may read and write files in C:\Users\billg\.claude in any session. Make a .bak copy first and log the change in WorkPlan.md. Scope is that folder only and does not cover deleting files.
rules.GR-20: Mandatory on every project: at the start of any work read E:\Dev\Claude\CLAUDE.md, follow it, then read the project's own CLAUDE.md.
rules.GR-21: Any new project or scaffold request means the newproject skill (E:\Dev\Claude\Skill\newproject). Read it first.
rules.GR-22: Every scaffold or audit lists E:\Dev as the resource parent directory in CLAUDE.md and in .claude\settings.json permissions.additionalDirectories.
rules.GR-24: One WorkPlan.md per project. No TODO.md, TASKS.md or todo.txt.
rules.GR-25: Default file location is E:\Dev\Claude, or the project's own folder under E:\Dev. Never save to the Cowork session output folder.
rules.GR-26: Memory routing: conventions go in CLAUDE.md, credentials and personal preferences go in session memory. Apply automatically.
rules.GR-27: Before every commit: update WorkPlan.md, Features.md and Specifications.md. Check the staged diff for secrets. Stage no logs, temp or *.key files.
rules.GR-28: Never commit API keys or key files (E:\Dev\.Anthropic.key, E:\Dev\.ClaudMCP.key). Load them from the environment.
rules.GR-29: Platform default is Windows 11 for paths, scripts and commands unless stated otherwise.
rules.GR-34: Handoff contract: read AGENTS.md first, preserve existing work, record every action in WorkPlan, state uncertainty plainly, report exact verification evidence.
rules.GR-48: Always use the E: drive (E:\Dev) for projects, files and folders. The H: drive is a backup drive only: never create or work in H:\Dev, and use H: only for backup copies (see GR-35 and GR-36).
rules.GR-49: When Bill asks for a project dashboard, build ONE central HTML dashboard for the project that covers all areas of the project (status, work items, tests, release, docs, devices, pre-production setups) and links to the project's other dashboards and artifacts. Global rules do not go on a project dashboard; they have their own independent dashboard in E:\Dev\Claude.
rules.GR-50: Every project that is attached and knows about the global rules must REREAD them every day (E:\Dev\Claude\GlobalRules.md, E:\Dev\AGENTS.md, C:\Users\billg\.claude\CLAUDE.md), check what changed since the last read, and APPLY every new or changed rule to the project (WorkPlan, docs, dashboards, tests, handoff). Log each daily check in the project's WorkPlan.md with the date and what changed, or 'no changes'. ENFORCEMENT: the recheck fires automatically whenever the handoff fires (GR-30/32, i.e. on every git save or WorkPlan update) via python E:\Dev\Claude\gr-recheck.py <project dir>, which compares the three files with the project .gr-stamp.json and logs the result in WorkPlan.md; a daily scheduled task is the backstop.
rules.GR-51: Every project in E:\Dev is attached to the central Claude.md, no exceptions. The main Claude.md is E:\Dev\Claude\CLAUDE.md (together with E:\Dev\Claude\GlobalRules.md); there is no E:\Dev\Claude.md and no other location may be named as the main Claude.md. Each project's CLAUDE.md carries the 'Attached to the central Claude.md' block (AUTO:CENTRALCLAUDE) and its ProjectInfo.md carries the global-rules block (AUTO:GLOBALRULES), and the attachment is logged in the project's WorkPlan.md. The newproject skill (new project scaffold AND audit mode) always adds this attachment when scaffolding. Refresh every project with E:\Python\Python314\python.exe -I E:\Dev\DevOps\allprojects\sync-projectinfo-globalrules.py.
rules.GR-52: If Claude cannot write to Bill's PC (folder not connected, access denied, PC offline), write to the repo instead; never skip the write. Use the project's repo, else the private FriesianLogic/ClaudeSkills repo. Log in the project's WorkPlan.md what was written and where, and merge it to the PC copy once the PC is reachable. Repos stay PRIVATE (GR-42); for local-only repos (GR-35/36) hold the content in ClaudeSkills/pending/ instead.
rules.GR-53: For ALL chats and ALL projects, always save the chat session conversation to a chat history file for reference. Each project has its OWN separate file: <project dir>\ChatHistory\ChatHistory.md (chats with no project: E:\Dev\Claude\ChatHistory\General.md). Append each session as a dated section (requests, what was done, decisions, outcomes, open items). Never mix projects in one file. Never record secrets, keys, card or ID numbers (GR-28). Falls back to the repo when the PC is not writable (GR-52).
rules.GR-54: When Bill's message contains two or more tasks, requests or commands - however casually written, in any chat or project - Claude AUTOMATICALLY, without being asked: (1) extracts EVERY task into a numbered checklist (task list widget / WorkPlan.md per GR-04); (2) treats the message as carrying an implicit 'do not stop until all N are done' - no need for Bill to say it - and works through every item without stopping or handing back partway, until all N are complete or a real blocker (usage/tokens) is reported (GR-03, GR-45); (3) adds a final verify task and ends the reply with a pass/fail line per numbered item, listing anything not done with a 'Fix It All' option. A task is never dropped silently: if blocked, say which number and why, then continue with the rest.
rules.GR-55: Whenever Claude notices (by its own check, an audit, or Bill saying so) that a task was skipped or missed, Claude does NOT ask and does NOT stop the current work: it immediately runs the missed task in the background (subagent, background process, or send_later/scheduled task - whichever the surface offers) while the current task continues, then reports the missed item and its result in the next pass/fail line (GR-54). If it truly cannot be run in the background, it queues it as the next numbered item and keeps going.
rules.GR-56: Chat history is how Claude avoids repeat mistakes (extends GR-53). (1) At the START of every session and every project task, Claude reads that project's ChatHistory\ChatHistory.md (E:\Dev\Claude\ChatHistory\General.md for no-project chats), checks the latest sessions for open items, missed tasks and past mistakes, and runs any unfinished item per GR-55. (2) Claude appends to the history DURING the session after each completed task (not only at the end) so nothing is lost if the chat stops. (3) When Bill reports a mistake, Claude records it in that project's ChatHistory under 'Mistakes and lessons' with the fix, and applies the lesson from then on. Secrets are never recorded (GR-28).
rules.GR-57: Standard 3-step workflow on EVERY request, in every chat and project, no exceptions (combines GR-54, GR-55, GR-56). STEP 1 CHECKLIST: as the first action, list every task in Bill's message as a numbered checklist (task list widget, and the project WorkPlan.md per GR-04) and work all of them to the end without stopping or handing back. STEP 2 HISTORY: before starting, read the project's ChatHistory\ChatHistory.md (E:\Dev\Claude\ChatHistory\General.md when no project) for open items, missed tasks and lessons; run anything missed in the background without asking; append to the history after each completed task and record any mistake under 'Mistakes and lessons'. STEP 3 VERIFY: before finishing, check every item against evidence (open the file, run the check) and end the reply with a pass/fail line per numbered item; anything not done is listed with a 'Fix It All' option. If any step is skipped, say which rule and why in the same reply (GR-23). ENFORCED BY: the 'Standard workflow' block at the top of E:\Dev\Claude\CLAUDE.md and C:\Users\billg\.claude\CLAUDE.md, the same block in every project's CLAUDE.md (AUTO:CENTRALCLAUDE, GR-51), and the UserPromptSubmit hook C:\Users\billg\.claude\hooks\three-step.ps1 that injects this reminder plus the project's recent chat history on every prompt in Claude Code (Stop hook GR-45 blocks finishing with open goal items).
rules.GR-30: Whenever work is saved to git or the WorkPlan is updated, ALSO refresh the project's session handoff note (for example SessionHandoff.md), in the background. The handoff refresh ALSO runs the GR-50 global-rules recheck: python E:\Dev\Claude\gr-recheck.py <project dir> --trigger handoff (a git post-commit hook fires it on every commit).
rules.GR-31: At the end of each work night: push to git, save, and update the web page or published output.
rules.GR-32: Trigger phrases "Save session" or "Save handoff": immediately update WorkPlan.md, refresh SessionHandoff.md (repo copy, project doc, PC copy) and push to git. Skill: save-handoff.
rules.GR-33: Every Friesian Logic app follows the HealthLive onboarding, Terms, Privacy and subscription pattern in E:\Dev\Standards\FriesianLogic_Onboarding_Standard.md.
rules.GR-35: AboutMe and Personal Dashboard repos stay local only. Never upload them to GitHub. Back them up to the H: drive instead.
rules.GR-36: Other local repos are also copied to the H: backup. Do not remove local repos. Do not push personal repos to GitHub.
rules.GR-45: When Bill sets a goal, Claude keeps working on all the tasks and work needed until the goal is reached and never stops partway. The only exception is running out of usage or tokens. Enforced in Claude Code by a Stop hook (goal-stop.ps1, settings.json) that blocks stopping while E:\Dev\ACTIVE_GOAL.md has open "- [ ]" items; in chat by a task list plus a send_later check-in. Every Stop/StopFailure event is logged to E:\Dev\StopHookFailures.md.
rules.GR-37: When testing, keep adb port setups (emulator console and adb ports, adb tcpip, adb connect, -port, adb server port) within the recommended ranges. Do not pick arbitrary ports. Range per the emulator's own warning: adb port 5555-5586 (console port even, 5554-5584; adb = console + 1).
rules.GR-38: Keep GlobalRules.md synced with every global rule Bill creates, and keep GlobalRules.html rebuilt.
rules.GR-39: Build and maintain E:\Dev\AllProjects.md ongoing: dashboards used, web-published services, cloud configuration and setup requirements per project, logged in each project's ProjectInfo.md and cataloged in AllProjects.md. Refresh with scan-projects.ps1, firstpass.py, gen-projectinfo-html.py, build-html.py (E:\Dev\DevOps\allprojects).
rules.GR-40: Every project folder in E:\Dev has a ProjectInfo.html. Create it if missing. Never overwrite an existing one.
rules.GR-41: Test Manager: Test runs: every test run being executed is registered FIRST with the global Test Manager (E:\Dev\TestManager.md, tm.py register) and ALSO in that project's own ProjectInfo.md and WorkPlan.md (tm.py register does all three). End it when finished (tm.py end, which logs the result in all three). Record project, what is tested, owner, launcher, programs, ports (GR-37 range) and resources. Claude surveys with tm.py survey. ENFORCED by DevOps: scheduled task 'TestManager Survey' runs tm.py survey every 5 minutes and AUTO-REGISTERS any test run that was not registered (also in the project's ProjectInfo.md and WorkPlan.md) and AUTO-CLOSES finished ones; scripted runs should use `tm.py run --project P --what "..." -- <command>` which registers, runs and always ends the entry.
rules.GR-42: All repos are created and managed as PRIVATE by default. Never create a public repo or change visibility to public unless Bill explicitly asks for that specific repo.
rules.GR-43: Every project's testing must conform to the Test Manager requirements and rules (E:\Dev\TestManager.md, Rules section): register before starting, state resources, ports inside the GR-37 range, close the entry when done, never stop another project's run without Bill's go-ahead, unknown values written as "not recorded". Non-conforming runs are flagged by the survey.
rules.GR-44: Test Manager lists every test cycle separately: when a project runs several tests at once, each test cycle gets its own row with its purpose, status, ports and processes (Test cycles per project table in TestManager.md, rebuilt by tm.py survey). When registering, give each cycle its own purpose.
rules.GR-46: Standard test automation setup: every Android-capable project is tested across the portfolio of 15 device profiles (Pixel 6, Small phone, 7.6in foldable, Tablet, Galaxy S25 / S25 Ultra / S25 FE / S26 FE / S26+ / Z Fold7 / Z Flip7 / Z Flip7 FE, moto g play / power / stylus) on Android 14, 15, 16 and 17 (API 34-37) = 60 emulator cells, using the proven HealthLive matrix kit (E:\Dev\HealthLive\tools\emulator-matrix). AVDs named <PREFIX>_<DEVICE>_<API>; ports in the GR-37 range; smoke per cell = boot, install, first-run flow, 500 monkey taps, crash check; Android 17 needs the SystemUI-disabled workaround; every run registered with the Test Manager (GR-41/43/44). Each project records its plan and all test actions in its own ProjectTestManager.md (template: E:\Dev\RainDrops\ProjectTestManager.md).
rules.GR-47: All test management follows E:\Dev\TestManager.md (standard suite, device portfolio of 15 profiles, Android 14-17 scope, lessons) and is done with the global testautomation skill and kit (E:\Dev\TestAutomation, private repo FriesianLogic/TestAutomation). A new project told to use the skill or kit is onboarded with kit\New-TestProject.ps1, runs canary then smoke/full via kit\Invoke-TestRun.ps1 and gets a production-readiness verdict. Every project, scaffolded by the newproject skill every time, has a ProjectTestManager.md.
